key_insight: The paper presents an open-source stereolithography workflow for making transparent 3D-printed porous flow cells, enabling direct imaging and pressure measurements of multiphase flow in designed micro- to millimetre-scale geometries.
engineering_relevance: This fabrication protocol lowers the barrier to building custom optically accessible porous-media experiments for studying flow, mixing, transport, and multiphase behavior.
method: Digitally design monolithic porous flow cells and print them by stereolithography.
Flush internal channels to remove uncured resin from enclosed voids.
Apply resin coating to make the printed cells optically transparent for imaging.
evidence_signal: The proof-of-concept compares oil-air two-phase flow reversal in triangular versus cylindrical obstacle cells using pressure data and image-based active-width measurements.
watch_item: Performance depends on successful internal flushing and coating; incomplete resin removal or inconsistent transparency could affect imaging quality and repeatability.
paper_title: Transparent 3D-printed flow cells for porous media studies with proof-of-concept on two-phase flow-reversal asymmetry
